name: Saladin Abolishes the Fatimid Caliphate
summary: Saladin, who had been sent to Egypt as the Fatimid vizier by Nur ad-Din of Syria, used his position to undermine the Ismaili Shia Fatimid caliphate. When the last Fatimid caliph Al-Adid died in September 1171, Saladin simply omitted his name from the Friday sermon, restoring the Sunni Abbasid caliph's name. Egypt returned to Sunni Islam; Saladin's Ayyubid dynasty replaced the Fatimid administration.
outcomes: Last Fatimid caliph dies; no successor named
Egypt returns to Sunni Abbasid allegiance

_quarry.structural_significance: Ended two centuries of Fatimid Ismaili rule in Egypt; unified Syria and Egypt under Saladin and created the strategic base for Crusader reconquest.
